# Glossary

Every mechanic word used anywhere in the book is defined here, once, from the
reader's question rather than the mechanism. Pages link to it with
`[[term]]`. An entry that can only be written in mechanism words marks a term
that does not belong in Part I.

## A

### allowance

How many sends one mailbox may make per day. When a mailbox spends its
allowance, it does not error; it waits until your local midnight and starts
again. Give two mailboxes different allowances and the daemon spreads work
between them by itself.

More: [mailboxes](../part-ii/12-account.md), [sending](../part-ii/15-sending.md)

## B

### batch

A group of jobs created together from one file or one campaign. The batch is
how you see and steer work as a group: approve it, pause it, read its totals.

More: [batches](../part-ii/14c-show-list.md), [approve](../part-ii/14b-approve.md)

See also: [[job]]

## C

### code

The one-word reason a send failed, as the failed screen shows it. Every code
has a plain meaning; the complete list lives in the
[failed command chapter](../part-ii/24-failed.md).

See also: [[failed]]

## F

### failed

A send that could not be delivered, with the reason recorded. A failed job is
kept, not thrown away, and it will try again on its own within the retry
rules unless the reason says the mailbox or the address made that pointless.

More: [the failed command](../part-ii/24-failed.md), [why things fail](32-failures.md)

See also: [[job]], [[code]]

## J

### job

One email that downcroc has been asked to send, together with everything it
needs: the recipient, the subject, the body, and the record of what happened
when it tried. A job is the unit you create, watch, and cancel. It exists
before it is sent and after, so the history is always readable.

More: [jobs](../part-ii/14d-jobs.md)

See also: [[queued]], [[sent]], [[failed]], [[batch]]

## Q

### queued

Written down and waiting. A queued job has everything it needs; it is not
sending yet, either because you have not told it to or because its turn has
not come. Nothing is wrong with a queued job.

More: [job states](33-states.md)

See also: [[job]], [[sent]]

## S

### sent

The receiving mail server accepted the message. Accepted is the honest word:
it does not promise a human read it, and it does not promise delivery to the
inbox, only that the server took it.

More: [job states](33-states.md)

See also: [[job]], [[queued]]

## V

### vault

The encrypted store that holds your mailboxes' credentials. It is locked when
the daemon is not running, unlocked while it works, and locked again on a
clean stop. A locked vault is normal; nothing sends until it is unlocked.

More: [vault commands](../part-ii/11-vault.md)
